newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end sharply off after recent rise.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end sharply off after recent rise.

text.p: Hong Kong's blue chips snapped a seven-day winning streak on Friday to end sharply lower, as the market took a well-earned rest from its recent ascent.
The Hang Seng index closed 109.05 points lower at 11,905.51 on turnover of HK$6.87 billion versus Thursday's 7.85 billion. Despite Friday's drop, the index rose 146 points over the week.
However, China shares picked up the lead and rallied to a strong close. The H-share index gained 15.05 points to 833.89.
"We have moved up very strongly and any consolidation would be healthy to provide a base for a trading range," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities.
"The only excitement in this market is anything China-related is just going through the roof," he added.
Analysts said there was some caution ahead of Friday's U.S. September employment data. Economists expect September payrolls to rise 166,000.
"Everything obviously is being based on the figures that are coming out of the U.S. I think we are just biding our time," said Remington.

Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said investors were taking profits ahead of the data. "I think basically we are seeing caution ahead of the weekend." Analysts said they expected stocks to pause awhile before resuming their upward trend.
HSBC Holdings shares took a sharp hit, falling HK$2.50 to HK$143.50.
"HSBC is pretty weak but it has had some very strong sessions," said Hutcheson. "It's pretty much across the board," he said of Friday's blue chip decline.
In the property sector, Cheung Kong fell HK$1.00 to HK$59.25 but Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.00 to HK$82.50.
Shares of casual wear maker and retailer Glorious Sun rose HK$0.45 to HK$3.85 and clothing wholesaler First Sign International gained HK$0.10 to HK$2.275.
"There is a belief that Chinese consumption is going to be picking up," said Remington.
Shares in China Travel rose HK$0.05 to HK$2.625 and Guangzhou Investment added HK$0.025 to HK$2.65.
"PRC interest rates are actually coming down and some companies will actually benefit from that," said Hutcheson.
October Hang Seng futures fell 85 points to 11,865.
